Now I can see the paper visually. Let me analyze what I see across pages 1-5:

**Page 1**: Title page with abstract and introduction. Clean layout, ACL format with line numbers. Title: "Phase-Modulated Compound Sparsity: Strategy-Dependent Severity Gradients in Reasoning Models". Anonymous ACL submission. Two-column format. Looks good.

**Page 2**: Background/Problem Setup and Experimental Setup sections. Contains equations (1) and (2). Clean formatting. No obvious issues.

**Page 3**: Results section with Table 1 and Figure 1. 
- Table 1 shows median compound severity difference. Clean formatting.


- Figure 1 displays the severity gradient across sparsity levels with two conditions (Importance and Random) and their confidence intervals clearly marked.
- Footnotes document the float16 to bfloat16 conversion and GPU specifications.

**Page 4**: Contains Table 2 with detailed breakdown and Table 3 showing Cohen's d values with confidence intervals, followed by the Discussion section. Table 2 is well-formatted, though Table 3's columns appear slightly compressed, particularly the CI columns, and there's some minor text overlap with adjacent content.

Looking more closely at Table 3, I'm checking the specific values and layout—the header shows sparsity level, DS effect size and confidence interval, and QW effect size and confidence interval. The data rows include the effect sizes and their bounds, with a superscript note indicating marginal significance at lower sparsity and reliable effects at higher levels. The rightmost column appears to extend close to the Discussion header, though it doesn't seem to actually overlap into that section.

Scanning through the rest of the document, I notice the Discussion section has normal hyphenation where words break across columns, which is standard for two-column ACL formatting. The Limitations section on page 5 is thorough, covering model scale, task coverage, mechanism, and sparsity range—good acknowledgment of the work's constraints. The overall layout is clean and follows proper conference formatting.
